data.assessment:
The attacker can read the partner application's stdout or log store. For example, they may be a log-platform user, support staff or an intruder on that system. They do not hold the partner secret. After any SDK call they copy the logged `Signature`, `Partner-Code`, `X-PP-Date` and `Content-MD5` values and the URL. They then send a request to that path before the backend's timestamp window closes. If the backend checks the body against `Content-MD5`, they also need the original body, which is not logged. If the backend trusts the header, any body is accepted. The backend is not in this repository, so the report does not say how long the window is or whether the body is checked. The SDK gives the integrator no way to turn the logging off.

Impact: While a logged signature is fresh, the attacker can replay signed calls such as `createpolicy` or `policystatus` as the partner. They cannot forge new signatures, and the long-term partner secret is not printed. How far this reaches depends on the backend's timestamp window and body check, which the report does not verify.
data.description:
Anyone who can read a partner application's stdout or log store can copy per-request authentication values written by the Ruby SDK and replay signed calls as that partner. They cannot forge new signatures, and the replay works only while the backend accepts the logged timestamp. The cause is `RequestManager#call_network`, which runs `puts hmac.hmac` and installs `faraday.response :logger` with no options.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  n1["attacker with log access"]
  n2["stdout and log pipeline"]
  n3["RequestManager call_network"]
  n4["signed partner requests (Signature, Partner-Code, X-PP-Date, Content-MD5)"]
  n5["opt-in logger with header redaction"]
  n3 -->|"writes HMAC and headers"| n2
  n1 -->|"reads logged values"| n2
  n1 -->|"replays while timestamp is fresh"| n4
  n5 -->|"not present"| n3
  classDef actor stroke:#2563eb,stroke-width:2px
  classDef vulnerable_code stroke:#dc2626,stroke-width:2px
  classDef existing_control stroke:#16a34a,stroke-width:2px
  classDef missing_control stroke:#dc2626,stroke-width:2px,stroke-dasharray:5 5
  classDef asset stroke:#9333ea,stroke-width:2px
  classDef component stroke:#6b7280,stroke-width:1px
  class n1 actor
  class n2 component
  class n3 vulnerable_code
  class n4 asset
  class n5 missing_control
```

1. **partner application** calls a public SDK method. `Policy.create_policy` and `Policy.get_policy_status` both go through `RequestManager#post` to `call_network`, so every SDK call reaches the logging code. ([`pasarpolis-sdk-ruby/lib/pasarpolis/policy.rb:17-66`](https://github.com/sprindigo-art/pasarpolis/blob/7355fb55a3e65c0166bf31cab81923d5519a83d9/pasarpolis-sdk-ruby/lib/pasarpolis/policy.rb#L17-L66))
2. **`call_network`** prints the raw HMAC signature. `puts hmac.hmac` has no condition, so each request's HMAC-SHA256 signature goes to stdout. ([`pasarpolis-sdk-ruby/lib/pasarpolis/request/request_manager.rb:33`](https://github.com/sprindigo-art/pasarpolis/blob/7355fb55a3e65c0166bf31cab81923d5519a83d9/pasarpolis-sdk-ruby/lib/pasarpolis/request/request_manager.rb#L33))
3. **Faraday logger middleware** logs the URL and all request and response headers to stdout. `faraday.response :logger` is given no logger or options. In Faraday 0.9.x-0.17.x this creates `Logger.new($stdout)` at DEBUG level, which dumps the headers. Request bodies are not logged. ([`pasarpolis-sdk-ruby/lib/pasarpolis/request/request_manager.rb:36-40`](https://github.com/sprindigo-art/pasarpolis/blob/7355fb55a3e65c0166bf31cab81923d5519a83d9/pasarpolis-sdk-ruby/lib/pasarpolis/request/request_manager.rb#L36-L40))
4. **request headers** carry the full authentication material into the logs. The header hash holds `Signature` (base64 of `partner_code:hmac`), `Partner-Code`, `X-PP-Date` and `Content-MD5`. ([`pasarpolis-sdk-ruby/lib/pasarpolis/request/request_manager.rb:43-52`](https://github.com/sprindigo-art/pasarpolis/blob/7355fb55a3e65c0166bf31cab81923d5519a83d9/pasarpolis-sdk-ruby/lib/pasarpolis/request/request_manager.rb#L43-L52))
5. **attacker** copies the logged values and sends a request to the same path. The signature covers only the verb, `Content-MD5`, content type, `X-PP-Date` and path, so the logged header set authenticates a request to that path while the backend accepts the timestamp. ([`pasarpolis-sdk-ruby/lib/pasarpolis/auth/hmac_auth.rb:22-26`](https://github.com/sprindigo-art/pasarpolis/blob/7355fb55a3e65c0166bf31cab81923d5519a83d9/pasarpolis-sdk-ruby/lib/pasarpolis/auth/hmac_auth.rb#L22-L26))
data.recommendation:
Debug output left in shipped code writes request authentication headers to the host application's stdout on every call. `puts hmac.hmac` prints the signature, and `faraday.response :logger` uses a default Faraday logger writing to `$stdout` at DEBUG. The integrator cannot turn this off.

Fix criteria: No default SDK code path prints or logs the `Signature`, `Content-MD5`, `X-PP-Date` or `Partner-Code` values or the HMAC. Any request logging is opt-in through an integrator-supplied logger and redacts those headers. To verify, run one `Policy.create_policy` and one `Policy.get_policy_status` call with default configuration. Confirm that stdout contains none of those values.
data.title: Ruby SDK logs per-request HMAC signature and auth headers to stdout

data.assessment:
The attacker is anyone able to read the repository, which the threat model lists as the actor "anyone reading the public repo". The same data also reaches anyone who receives the SDK, because partners are told to copy it. No credentials, requests or victim action are needed. The data is in a single checked-in commit, so it persists while the repository or any fork or clone is reachable.

Impact: The reader gets one insured person's name, date of birth, driving-licence number, vehicle VIN, engine number, plate and a family member's name. That is enough for identity or vehicle-related fraud against that person, and it is a reportable personal-data breach for the owner. Only one record is exposed, and nothing is modified or made unavailable.
data.description:
Anyone who can read the public repository, or who receives the SDK, can see one real insured driver's identity and vehicle record. It includes the person's name, date of birth, driving-licence number, vehicle VIN, engine number, plate and a child's name. The example payloads in `pasarpolis-sdk-python/example/example.py` (lines 26 and 35) hold a real record that was only partly anonymised. The exposure covers one record, not the policy database.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  n1["anyone reading the public repo"]
  n2["partner receiving the SDK copy"]
  n3["example.py go-car-simple payloads (lines 26 and 35)"]
  n4["insured driver's identity and vehicle record"]
  n5["check against real data in commits"]
  n1 -->|"reads the file in the repository"| n3
  n2 -->|"reads the copy shipped in the SDK"| n3
  n3 -->|"contains the record in plain text"| n4
  n5 -->|"not applied at commit"| n3
  classDef actor stroke:#2563eb,stroke-width:2px
  classDef vulnerable_code stroke:#dc2626,stroke-width:2px
  classDef existing_control stroke:#16a34a,stroke-width:2px
  classDef missing_control stroke:#dc2626,stroke-width:2px,stroke-dasharray:5 5
  classDef asset stroke:#9333ea,stroke-width:2px
  classDef component stroke:#6b7280,stroke-width:1px
  class n1 actor
  class n2 actor
  class n3 vulnerable_code
  class n4 asset
  class n5 missing_control
```

1. **the example author** pastes a real insured driver's request body into the `go-car-simple` validate-policy example. The literal JSON string holds the full name, date of birth, driving-licence number, VIN, engine number, plate and a nominee declared as the insured's child, and these values agree with each other the way real data does. ([`pasarpolis-sdk-python/example/example.py:26`](https://github.com/sprindigo-art/pasarpolis/blob/7355fb55a3e65c0166bf31cab81923d5519a83d9/pasarpolis-sdk-python/example/example.py#L26))
2. **the example author** copies the same record byte for byte into the create-policy example. The second copy means the data sits in two places in the same file. ([`pasarpolis-sdk-python/example/example.py:35`](https://github.com/sprindigo-art/pasarpolis/blob/7355fb55a3e65c0166bf31cab81923d5519a83d9/pasarpolis-sdk-python/example/example.py#L35))
3. **the example author** masks only some fields. `handphone` became a placeholder and `email` a staff address, and `uuid` and `vehicle_plate` are overwritten at runtime. The name, date of birth, licence number, VIN, engine number, plate and the child's name stay in the committed literal. ([`pasarpolis-sdk-python/example/example.py:28-29`](https://github.com/sprindigo-art/pasarpolis/blob/7355fb55a3e65c0166bf31cab81923d5519a83d9/pasarpolis-sdk-python/example/example.py#L28-L29))
4. **a repository reader** opens `pasarpolis-sdk-python/example/example.py` and reads lines 26 or 35. No login, request or victim action is needed, and the data stays in the commit for as long as the repository or any fork or clone is reachable.
5. **a partner** receives the file inside the SDK copy. The `README.md` "Installation Steps" tell partners to copy the SDK, so the exposure is not limited to the Git host.
data.recommendation:
(1) A real customer's request body was pasted into `pasarpolis-sdk-python/example/example.py` as the sample payload and only partly anonymised. Personal identifiers are stored in a publicly readable source file.

Fix criteria: The example payloads in `pasarpolis-sdk-python/example/example.py` contain only obviously synthetic values, such as `John Doe`, all-zero or `x`-masked identifiers and an invalid-checksum VIN. No identity-document, vehicle or family-member value can be traced to a person. A repository-wide search for the clan name, the `7402…` licence prefix, the `MHKA6…` VIN and the `3NR…` engine number returns nothing. The record is already in a public commit, so it is also purged from history, or the repository is re-published without it. The applicable personal-data-breach procedure is followed for the data subject.

(2) Nothing stops real customer data from being committed as fixtures or examples. Sibling fixtures show the same practice of copying payloads from traffic and masking them by hand.

Fix criteria: Example and test payloads across the SDKs come from a documented synthetic dataset. A pre-commit or CI check blocks commits that introduce such values. It is a secret/PII scanner with patterns for Indonesian SIM/KTP numbers, VINs, plates and e-mail addresses. Attempting to commit the current line 26 payload is rejected.
data.title: Real customer identity and vehicle record committed in Python SDK example payload

data.assessment:
The attacker is an unauthenticated peer with access to the internal network, where the stats endpoints are reachable. No login is needed. They send many concurrent requests to `GET /stats` or `POST /identifier-lookup`. They cannot make jobs fail themselves. A job enqueued with `retry` set to true or to an int must fail by panicking while a request is reading its message, and the attacker must win that timing race. Job functions also receive the `*Msg` and may write it, which gives another source of writes. Polling at a high rate raises the odds each time a retry-enabled job fails, and the attack can be repeated.

Impact: The worker binary exits and processing of every queue it serves stops until it is restarted. Messages left in the `inprogress` lists are re-run on restart through `processOldMessages`, so jobs that were mid-execution run twice and non-idempotent side effects can repeat. The race itself discloses no data.
data.description:
An unauthenticated peer on the internal network can crash the whole worker process and stop every queue it serves, by sending many concurrent requests to the stats endpoints. This is a timing race, so it is probabilistic but repeatable. It needs a retry-enabled job to fail while a request is reading it. The stats handlers read the live `*Msg` map while `MiddlewareRetry.Call` writes it, with no lock.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  n1["unauthenticated network peer"]
  n2["StatsServer handlers /stats and /identifier-lookup"]
  n3["in-flight Msg map"]
  n4["MiddlewareRetry.Call"]
  n5["worker process"]
  n6["lock or snapshot of the message"]
  n1 -->|"sends many concurrent requests"| n2
  n2 -->|"reads and iterates unlocked"| n3
  n4 -->|"writes on job panic"| n3
  n3 -->|"overlap makes runtime exit"| n5
  n6 -->|"not applied"| n2
  classDef actor stroke:#2563eb,stroke-width:2px
  classDef vulnerable_code stroke:#dc2626,stroke-width:2px
  classDef existing_control stroke:#16a34a,stroke-width:2px
  classDef missing_control stroke:#dc2626,stroke-width:2px,stroke-dasharray:5 5
  classDef asset stroke:#9333ea,stroke-width:2px
  classDef component stroke:#6b7280,stroke-width:1px
  class n1 actor
  class n2 vulnerable_code
  class n3 component
  class n4 component
  class n5 asset
  class n6 missing_control
```

1. **worker goroutine** publishes the running job as `worker.currentMsg`. The pointer is set before the middleware chain runs and cleared only after it returns, with no lock or atomic guarding it or the message contents. ([`go-workers/worker.go:29-37`](https://github.com/sprindigo-art/pasarpolis/blob/7355fb55a3e65c0166bf31cab81923d5519a83d9/go-workers/worker.go#L29-L37))
2. **attacker** floods `GET /stats` or `POST /identifier-lookup` with many concurrent requests. `StatsServer` serves both on all interfaces with no authentication, and the redigo pool sets only `MaxIdle`, so many concurrent requests are accepted. ([`go-workers/workers.go:98-108`](https://github.com/sprindigo-art/pasarpolis/blob/7355fb55a3e65c0166bf31cab81923d5519a83d9/go-workers/workers.go#L98-L108))
3. **stats handlers** read and serialize the live message map. `Stats` keeps the `worker.currentMsg` pointer and `json.MarshalIndent` iterates the map, while `IdentifierInQueue` reads it through `message.Args()` and `CheckGet("args")`. ([`go-workers/stats.go:29-39`](https://github.com/sprindigo-art/pasarpolis/blob/7355fb55a3e65c0166bf31cab81923d5519a83d9/go-workers/stats.go#L29-L39))
4. **`MiddlewareRetry.Call`** writes to the same map when a retry-enabled job panics. It calls `Set` for `queue` and `error_message`, and `incrementRetry` sets `failed_at`, `retried_at` and `retry_count`. This happens only if `retry` is true or an int below the max. ([`go-workers/middleware_retry.go:23-26`](https://github.com/sprindigo-art/pasarpolis/blob/7355fb55a3e65c0166bf31cab81923d5519a83d9/go-workers/middleware_retry.go#L23-L26))
5. **Go runtime** stops the whole worker process with a fatal error. A map read or iteration that overlaps a write calls `fatal`, which is not a panic, so neither `recover()` in `worker.process` nor the one in `net/http` catches it.
data.recommendation:
The HTTP handlers share the live, mutable `*Msg` (and `worker.currentMsg` and `startedAt`) with the worker goroutine without any synchronization, and `simplejson.Json` is not safe for concurrent read and write.

Fix criteria: The stats handlers never read a message that another goroutine may be writing. They serialize only an immutable snapshot (for example the original JSON string) taken under a lock or atomic when the worker starts a job. Running the test suite with `-race` while a stats request loops against panicking jobs gives no race report and no fatal error.
data.title: Stats handlers read in-flight job maps unsynchronized; concurrent retry writes crash worker process

data.assessment:
The attacker needs read access to the partner application's stdout or to the log store that collects it. That could be a log-platform user, support staff or an intruder on the log system. They do not need PasarPolis credentials. The attack also depends on the deployment keeping stdout and on the partner using products with the endorsement flow. Every status poll triggers the printing, and any 4xx or 5xx response also has its body printed by `call_network`. `setup.py` packages `pasarpolis` and `pasarpolis.request`, so every partner that installs the SDK gets these `print()` calls.

Impact: The attacker can read per-policy endorsement tokens, document links, activation links, policy and application numbers, partner references and coverage dates. The report does not show what a token or document link unlocks on the PasarPolis side, so it rates this as limited disclosure. The partner HMAC secret and request headers are not printed.
data.description:
Anyone who can read a partner application's stdout or log store can collect per-policy endorsement tokens and policy document links. The SDK writes them there on every status poll, and the SDK has no option to turn this off. The cause is leftover debug `print()` calls in `Policy.get_policy_status`, `Policy.get_policy_status_v3` and `RequestManager.call_network`.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  n1["log reader (platform user, support staff or intruder)"]
  n2["partner stdout and log store"]
  n3["get_policy_status and get_policy_status_v3 print calls"]
  n4["RequestManager.call_network print calls"]
  n5["endorsement tokens and document links"]
  n6["opt-in logging with redaction"]
  n1 -->|"reads logs"| n2
  n3 -->|"prints raw policy records"| n2
  n4 -->|"prints error response bodies"| n2
  n2 -->|"holds"| n5
  n6 -->|"not present, output always on"| n3
  classDef actor stroke:#2563eb,stroke-width:2px
  classDef vulnerable_code stroke:#dc2626,stroke-width:2px
  classDef existing_control stroke:#16a34a,stroke-width:2px
  classDef missing_control stroke:#dc2626,stroke-width:2px,stroke-dasharray:5 5
  classDef asset stroke:#9333ea,stroke-width:2px
  classDef component stroke:#6b7280,stroke-width:1px
  class n1 actor
  class n2 component
  class n3 vulnerable_code
  class n4 vulnerable_code
  class n5 asset
  class n6 missing_control
```

1. **partner application** polls policy status through the SDK. It calls `Policy.get_policy_status` or `Policy.get_policy_status_v3`, which fetch raw policy records from the API. ([`pasarpolis-sdk-python/pasarpolis/policy.py:229`](https://github.com/sprindigo-art/pasarpolis/blob/7355fb55a3e65c0166bf31cab81923d5519a83d9/pasarpolis-sdk-python/pasarpolis/policy.py#L229))
2. **the method `get_policy_status_v3`** prints each raw record to stdout. `print(policy)` runs before the record is mapped into a `Policy` object, so `endorsement_token`, `document_url`, `activation_url`, `policy_no` and `partner_ref` are all written out. ([`pasarpolis-sdk-python/pasarpolis/policy.py:229`](https://github.com/sprindigo-art/pasarpolis/blob/7355fb55a3e65c0166bf31cab81923d5519a83d9/pasarpolis-sdk-python/pasarpolis/policy.py#L229))
3. **the method `get_policy_status`** prints each raw record the same way. The printed record includes `endorsement_token` even though the returned `Policy` object never exposes it to the caller. ([`pasarpolis-sdk-python/pasarpolis/policy.py:187`](https://github.com/sprindigo-art/pasarpolis/blob/7355fb55a3e65c0166bf31cab81923d5519a83d9/pasarpolis-sdk-python/pasarpolis/policy.py#L187))
4. **the method `call_network`** prints the HTTP status of every call and the full body of error responses. On a 4xx or 5xx response it prints `res.text`. On success it prints only the response repr, such as `<Response [200]>`, so the partner secret and request headers are not written. ([`pasarpolis-sdk-python/pasarpolis/request/request_manager.py:55-62`](https://github.com/sprindigo-art/pasarpolis/blob/7355fb55a3e65c0166bf31cab81923d5519a83d9/pasarpolis-sdk-python/pasarpolis/request/request_manager.py#L55-L62))
5. **partner's log pipeline** captures stdout and stores the output. The report assumes the deployment keeps stdout. The printed tokens and links then sit in the log store.
6. **log reader** reads the tokens and document links from the logs. Log-platform users, support staff or an intruder on the log system can read them without holding any PasarPolis credentials.
data.recommendation:
Leftover debug `print()` calls in `policy.py:187`, `policy.py:229` and `request_manager.py:56-62` always write server response records and error bodies to the integrator's stdout. These records include per-policy tokens and document URLs.

Fix criteria: By default the SDK writes no response record, token, URL or error body to stdout or stderr. Any diagnostics are opt-in through a logger, with `endorsement_token`, `activation_url` and `document_url` redacted. Capture stdout while calling `get_policy_status`, `get_policy_status_v3` and a request that gets a 4xx response. Confirm that nothing is written.
data.title: Python SDK prints raw policy status records, including endorsement tokens, to stdout

data.assessment:
The attacker is a user of a partner application that calls a documented GET endpoint through `request.RequestManager{Params: ...}.Get()` and puts a value the user supplied into `Params`. Two preconditions are outside the attacker's control. The partner must use the SDK's GET path directly, because none of the bundled model functions do, and the partner must forward user input. The same flaw exists in both Go SDKs (`go-sdk.v2` and `go-sdk`). A copy in `GetQueryStringFromMap` aggregate code cannot be reached, because its only caller, `aggregateCallNetwork`, is unexported and only used with `POST`. Values containing `+`, `%`, spaces or non-ASCII characters are also corrupted or can make the request line invalid.

Impact: The attacker can change which records or options a partner GET request addresses, by adding, duplicating or cutting off query parameters. This stays within operations the partner account is already allowed to perform. The response goes back to the partner's code, not to the attacker, so the report establishes no disclosure, only a limited loss of integrity in the partner's API interaction.
data.description:
A user of a partner application can add, duplicate or cut off query parameters in a GET request that the partner's Go SDK signs and sends to the PasarPolis API. The attack needs the partner to call `RequestManager.Get()` directly and put user-supplied values into `Params`. The cause is `GetQueryStringFromMap` in both Go SDKs, which joins keys and values without percent-encoding them. Impact is limited to what the partner account may already do.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  n1["End user of partner app"]
  n2["RequestManager.Get with Params"]
  n3["GetQueryStringFromMap"]
  n4["percent-encoding of keys and values"]
  n5["Signed GET request to PasarPolis API"]
  n1 -->|"supplies value with ampersand, equals or hash"| n2
  n2 -->|"passes Params"| n3
  n3 -->|"builds altered query that gets signed and sent"| n5
  n4 -->|"not applied"| n3
  classDef actor stroke:#2563eb,stroke-width:2px
  classDef vulnerable_code stroke:#dc2626,stroke-width:2px
  classDef existing_control stroke:#16a34a,stroke-width:2px
  classDef missing_control stroke:#dc2626,stroke-width:2px,stroke-dasharray:5 5
  classDef asset stroke:#9333ea,stroke-width:2px
  classDef component stroke:#6b7280,stroke-width:1px
  class n1 actor
  class n2 component
  class n3 vulnerable_code
  class n4 missing_control
  class n5 asset
```

1. **End user of a partner app** submits a value containing `&`, `=` or `#`. An example is `x&application_number=<other>` or `x#`, sent to a partner feature that passes the value on in a GET call.
2. **Partner code** puts the value into `Params` and calls `RequestManager.Get()`. `callNetwork` hands the caller's `Params` to `GetQueryStringFromMap` for GET requests; the SDK has no model function for GET endpoints such as the claims benefits list, so partners call `Get()` directly. ([`go-sdk.v2/request/request_manager.go:70-73`](https://github.com/sprindigo-art/pasarpolis/blob/7355fb55a3e65c0166bf31cab81923d5519a83d9/go-sdk.v2/request/request_manager.go#L70-L73))
3. **`GetQueryStringFromMap`** joins every key and value into the query string without encoding. It concatenates `"&" + k + "=" + fmt.Sprint(v)`, so `&`, `=` and `#` in a value become query syntax. ([`go-sdk.v2/utils/map_utils.go:9-15`](https://github.com/sprindigo-art/pasarpolis/blob/7355fb55a3e65c0166bf31cab81923d5519a83d9/go-sdk.v2/utils/map_utils.go#L9-L15))
4. **`callNetwork`** assigns the string to `RawQuery` and creates the request with `http.NewRequest`. `http.NewRequest` re-parses the URL, so an injected `&` or `=` becomes a real parameter delimiter and everything after `#` is treated as a fragment and never sent. ([`go-sdk.v2/request/request_manager.go:98-112`](https://github.com/sprindigo-art/pasarpolis/blob/7355fb55a3e65c0166bf31cab81923d5519a83d9/go-sdk.v2/request/request_manager.go#L98-L112))
5. **PasarPolis API** receives the signed request with the altered query. The request carries the partner's signature headers but addresses different or extra parameters than the partner intended; Go's random map order decides whether a duplicated parameter comes first or last.
data.recommendation:
`GetQueryStringFromMap` in both Go SDKs builds query parameters by raw string concatenation with no percent-encoding. Caller values containing query metacharacters change the structure of the request URL.

Fix criteria: Each `Params` key and value is percent-encoded and sent as exactly one query parameter, for example with `url.Values.Encode()`. A test with a value containing `&`, `=`, `#`, `+` and a space shows the request line carries exactly one parameter whose decoded value matches the input. The same test shows no fragment truncation. Nested maps or slices have a defined encoding or are rejected, and are not rendered with `fmt.Sprint`.
data.title: Go SDK GET query string built without URL-encoding enables parameter injection

data.assessment:
The attacker is any peer that can reach the stats port. `StatsServer` listens on all interfaces with no authentication, and the README documents it as standard usage. No credentials are needed. The impact depends on the retry set being large. That is a runtime state the attacker does not control. Jobs enqueued with `retry` stay in the set while they keep failing, for up to 25 retries with `count^4` back-off, about 18 days. The code puts no bound on the set's size.

Impact: The worker process can be OOM-killed or stall, which stops job processing for every queue in that process while the attack lasts. The handler does not disclose or modify any data beyond its normal output.

Subsequent-system impact: Each request makes the shared, single-threaded Redis run an O(N) `ZRANGE` and send the whole set. Concurrent lookups can delay commands from other workers' fetchers and from the enqueuing application. The report establishes degradation of that shared service, not a guaranteed outage.
data.description:
Anyone who can reach the stats port can slow down or crash the worker process, and degrade the shared Redis, without logging in. Impact depends on the retry set being large, which the attacker does not control. `CheckIdentifierInRetry` reads and decodes the whole retry set for every `/identifier-lookup` request, and `StatsServer` puts no limit on how many requests run at once.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  n1["unauthenticated network peer"]
  n2["StatsServer /identifier-lookup"]
  n3["CheckIdentifierInRetry"]
```

1. **attacker** sends many concurrent `POST /identifier-lookup` requests with a nonexistent identifier. The body is like `{"queue":"x","identifier":"nonexistent"}`, and no credentials are needed. ([`go-workers/workers.go:98-108`](https://github.com/sprindigo-art/pasarpolis/blob/7355fb55a3e65c0166bf31cab81923d5519a83d9/go-workers/workers.go#L98-L108))
2. **the function `CheckQueueData`** finds no in-flight worker holding the identifier and falls through to the retry scan. A caller-chosen nonexistent identifier therefore always triggers the full-set scan. ([`go-workers/stats.go:93-111`](https://github.com/sprindigo-art/pasarpolis/blob/7355fb55a3e65c0166bf31cab81923d5519a83d9/go-workers/stats.go#L93-L111))
3. **the function `CheckIdentifierInRetry`** runs `ZRANGE <ns>goretry 0 -1` and decodes every member with `json.Unmarshal`. There is no LIMIT, cursor, size cap, cache or index, so each request copies the whole retry set into the worker's memory. ([`go-workers/stats.go:142-172`](https://github.com/sprindigo-art/pasarpolis/blob/7355fb55a3e65c0166bf31cab81923d5519a83d9/go-workers/stats.go#L142-L172))
4. **the Redis pool** gives each concurrent request its own new Redis connection. Only `MaxIdle` is set and `MaxActive` stays 0, which the report assumes means unlimited in redigo v1.6.4. ([`go-workers/config.go:51-53`](https://github.com/sprindigo-art/pasarpolis/blob/7355fb55a3e65c0166bf31cab81923d5519a83d9/go-workers/config.go#L51-L53))
5. **worker process and Redis** run out of memory or fall behind under the repeated full-set copies. Worker memory grows roughly as concurrency times retry-set size, and the single-threaded Redis must serialize and send the whole set for every request.
data.recommendation:
(1) `CheckIdentifierInRetry` does work and allocates memory in proportion to the whole retry set on every request, with no cap. The cost of one lookup depends on server state, not on the request.

Fix criteria: A single lookup does bounded work and allocates bounded memory whatever the retry-set size, for example through an identifier-to-job index or an incremental scan with a hard cap on elements examined and bytes held. With the retry set filled with many large entries, a lookup for a nonexistent identifier no longer issues `ZRANGE 0 -1`. Worker memory per request stays flat.

(2) `StatsServer` exposes the expensive lookup to any network peer with no authentication, rate limiting, timeouts or concurrency limit, and the Redis pool has no `MaxActive`. Concurrent requests multiply the cost without limit.

Fix criteria: Only authorized operators can call the lookup. Concurrent or repeated requests are bounded by rate and concurrency limits and server timeouts, and the Redis pool has a connection ceiling. A flood of unauthenticated or excess lookup requests is rejected before any Redis command runs. Worker memory and the Redis connection count stay bounded.
data.title: Unauthenticated identifier-lookup loads the whole Redis retry set on every request

data.assessment:
The attacker is any party who can open a TCP connection to the port of a worker running `workers.StatsServer`. This is the documented way to expose monitoring. No credential, victim action or bypassed defense is needed. A second route is a web page loaded in an internal user's browser. Both handlers answer simple GET or POST requests, skip the content type check and send `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`, so such a page can read the responses. For `/identifier-lookup` the attacker must supply a guessed `identifier`. For `/stats` the attacker only polls and sees the jobs in flight at that moment.

Impact: The attacker can read the full documents of jobs the worker is processing, including `args`, and can confirm guessed identifiers. They can also pull matching retry-set jobs with their handler error text, without Redis credentials. The handlers only read data, so nothing is changed. The report finds no way to cause denial of service, since the full retry-set scan only adds load.
data.description:
Anyone who can reach the worker's stats port can read the full contents of jobs being processed, including their arguments, which the report counts as insurance policy data and personal data. They can also check whether a guessed identifier appears in a job and pull failed jobs from the retry set. No login is needed. `workers.StatsServer` binds every interface with no authentication, and its handlers return raw job documents.

1. **integrator** starts the documented stats server. The README tells integrators to run `go workers.StatsServer(8080)` and gives no warning about network exposure or the need for authentication. ([`go-workers/README.md:69-71`](https://github.com/sprindigo-art/pasarpolis/blob/7355fb55a3e65c0166bf31cab81923d5519a83d9/go-workers/README.md#L69-L71))
2. **`StatsServer`** registers the handlers and listens on all interfaces. It registers `/stats` and `/identifier-lookup` on `http.DefaultServeMux` and calls `http.ListenAndServe` on `:port`, with no credential, allow-list or loopback restriction; its log lines advertise `http://localhost:<port>`. ([`go-workers/workers.go:98-108`](https://github.com/sprindigo-art/pasarpolis/blob/7355fb55a3e65c0166bf31cab81923d5519a83d9/go-workers/workers.go#L98-L108))
3. **network caller** sends `GET /stats` repeatedly. `Stats` adds each busy worker's `currentMsg` to the response and sends `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`, so every in-flight job is returned to any caller. ([`go-workers/stats.go:18-79`](https://github.com/sprindigo-art/pasarpolis/blob/7355fb55a3e65c0166bf31cab81923d5519a83d9/go-workers/stats.go#L18-L79))
4. **`Msg`** serialises the whole job document. `Msg` embeds `*data`, which embeds `*simplejson.Json`, so its promoted `MarshalJSON` emits the full job (`class`, `args`, `jid`, retry fields); this rests on the report's assumption about go-simplejson v0.5.1. ([`go-workers/msg.go:8-15`](https://github.com/sprindigo-art/pasarpolis/blob/7355fb55a3e65c0166bf31cab81923d5519a83d9/go-workers/msg.go#L8-L15))
5. **network caller** sends `POST /identifier-lookup` with a `queue` and a guessed `identifier`. `CheckQueueData` decodes the body without checking the method, content type, size or credentials. ([`go-workers/stats.go:93-140`](https://github.com/sprindigo-art/pasarpolis/blob/7355fb55a3e65c0166bf31cab81923d5519a83d9/go-workers/stats.go#L93-L140))
6. **`CheckIdentifierInRetry`** scans the `goretry` sorted set and returns the matching job. It reads the whole set with `ZRANGE 0 -1` and returns the full job as `message`, including the `error_message` that the retry middleware stored from the handler's panic text; a `status` of true also confirms the guess. ([`go-workers/stats.go:144-172`](https://github.com/sprindigo-art/pasarpolis/blob/7355fb55a3e65c0166bf31cab81923d5519a83d9/go-workers/stats.go#L144-L172))
data.recommendation:
(1) `workers.go:98-108` serves `/stats` and `/identifier-lookup` on all interfaces with no authentication or authorization. `stats.go:20` and `stats.go:95` allow any origin with `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`. Any network peer, or any page in an internal user's browser, can read job data.

Fix criteria: The documented server requires a valid operator credential, or binds only to loopback or an explicitly configured admin address, before either handler runs. It no longer sends `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`. `/identifier-lookup` accepts only its declared method and content type. An unauthenticated `GET /stats` and `POST /identifier-lookup` from a non-local address are rejected, with no job content in the body.

(2) `stats.go:34-37`, `stats.go:129-132` and `stats.go:164-166` serialise the entire `*Msg` or retry document, including `args` and `error_message`. `stats.go:108-110` marshals raw Redis errors. Even an authorised caller sees too much.

Fix criteria: Responses contain only operational metadata (jid, class, queue, started_at, counts). They never include raw `args` or handler error text, and internal errors are replaced by a generic message. A job with a distinctive argument value never appears in either response body.
data.title: Unauthenticated stats and identifier-lookup endpoints expose full job payloads

data.assessment:
The attacker is anyone who can read the public repository. They need no account, no privilege and no victim action. They copy the partner code and secret from `README.md`, sign requests the way `hmac_auth.php` and `request_manager.php` do, and send them to the publicly named testing host. The report does not say whether the key still works.

Impact: The attacker can act as partner `laku6` on the testing environment: read status records of its test policies, and create, cancel or terminate them. In the SDK repository itself, this is a limited loss of secrecy for a non-production credential. The SDK's own behaviour and availability do not change.

Subsequent-system impact: The effect lands on the PasarPolis integrations-testing API, where the attacker has the access of partner `laku6` with limited read and write reach over its test policies. The repository shows the impact only on the testing host, not on sandbox or production. A separate `umra` sandbox secret is hard-coded in `pasarpolis-sdk-php/example.php:6` and needs its own rotation.

1. **attacker** reads the public README. The Initialize example passes the partner code `laku6` and a 36-character UUID secret for `https://integrations-testing.pasarpolis.io`, and it is not a placeholder like the one on line 19. ([`pasarpolis-sdk-php/README.md:35`](https://github.com/sprindigo-art/pasarpolis/blob/7355fb55a3e65c0166bf31cab81923d5519a83d9/pasarpolis-sdk-php/README.md#L35))
2. **attacker** computes the request signature with the copied secret. The HMAC-SHA256 is keyed only by the partner secret, and the client chooses the timestamp, so the secret alone is enough to sign any request. ([`pasarpolis-sdk-php/pasarpolis/request/auth/hmac_auth.php:24-29`](https://github.com/sprindigo-art/pasarpolis/blob/7355fb55a3e65c0166bf31cab81923d5519a83d9/pasarpolis-sdk-php/pasarpolis/request/auth/hmac_auth.php#L24-L29))
3. **attacker** builds the `Signature` header as base64 of partner code, a colon and the HMAC. This header, sent with `Partner-Code`, `X-PP-Date` and `Content-MD5`, is the whole credential, so the attacker needs nothing else. ([`pasarpolis-sdk-php/pasarpolis/request/request_manager.php:29-38`](https://github.com/sprindigo-art/pasarpolis/blob/7355fb55a3e65c0166bf31cab81923d5519a83d9/pasarpolis-sdk-php/pasarpolis/request/request_manager.php#L29-L38))

data.recommendation:
The README embeds a real partner's HMAC secret for `laku6`, so the key is public and anyone can sign requests with it.

Fix criteria: The `laku6` secret is revoked or rotated, and the README uses a clearly fake placeholder. The old key is treated as burned, or history is scrubbed. No UUID-shaped literal remains next to `new client(` in the documentation.

data.assessment:
The attacker is anyone who can read the public repository. No account, victim action or special setup is needed. They copy a partner code and secret from `example.php` or `README.md`. They then sign requests with any SDK or by hand and send them over the internet. The attack works only if PasarPolis has not yet revoked these keys on the sandbox and testing hosts. The repository cannot show that server-side state.

Impact: The attacker gets partner-level API access as `umra` on sandbox and `laku6` on testing. They can create policies, cancel or terminate policies whose reference they know, and read policy status and document URLs. Both environments are non-production, so this is limited to test data, unless the same secrets are reused on production. The report does not say whether they are.

([`pasarpolis-sdk-php/example.php:6`](https://github.com/sprindigo-art/pasarpolis/blob/7355fb55a3e65c0166bf31cab81923d5519a83d9/pasarpolis-sdk-php/example.php#L6))
2. **attacker** takes the second partner credential from the README. The README example uses partner code `laku6` for `https://integrations-testing.pasarpolis.io`, while the same README shows a placeholder form on line 19. ([`pasarpolis-sdk-php/README.md:35`](https://github.com/sprindigo-art/pasarpolis/blob/7355fb55a3e65c0166bf31cab81923d5519a83d9/pasarpolis-sdk-php/README.md#L35))
3. **attacker** signs a request with the copied secret. `hmac_auth.php` uses the secret alone as the HMAC-SHA256 key over values the caller picks: verb, body MD5, content type, timestamp and path. ([`pasarpolis-sdk-php/pasarpolis/request/auth/hmac_auth.php:24-37`](https://github.com/sprindigo-art/pasarpolis/blob/7355fb55a3e65c0166bf31cab81923d5519a83d9/pasarpolis-sdk-php/pasarpolis/request/auth/hmac_auth.php#L24-L37))

([`pasarpolis-sdk-php/pasarpolis/request/request_manager.php:29-38`](https://github.com/sprindigo-art/pasarpolis/blob/7355fb55a3e65c0166bf31cab81923d5519a83d9/pasarpolis-sdk-php/pasarpolis/request/request_manager.php#L29-L38))

data.recommendation:
Real partner HMAC secrets for `umra` and `laku6` were committed in `example.php` and `README.md` instead of placeholders, so every reader of the repository holds the signing keys.

Fix criteria: The secrets for `umra` and `laku6` are rotated or revoked on every environment that accepts them, including production if they were reused there. `example.php` and `README.md`, and the git history, hold only obvious placeholders or values read from the environment. The old values no longer authenticate against the sandbox and testing hosts. A search of the repository for UUID-format strings passed to `client(` or `init(` finds no live secret.

data.assessment:
The attacker is anyone who can read the repository. No login, privilege or victim action is needed. They copy the partner code and secret from `go-sdk/test/models/policy_test.go` (or `go-sdk/test/pasarpolis_test.go`). They sign requests like `auth/hmac.go` does and send them to `integrations-testing.pasarpolis.com` over the internet. The leaked data is the partner's signing secret plus an apparent employee e-mail address (`neha.shrivastava@pasarpolis.com`), which is minor personal data. Subsequent-system impact: On the PasarPolis testing API the attacker acts as the internal `pasarpolis` partner, so they can read policy data and create policies. This is testing-environment data, and the code does not show the key is valid in production.

([`go-sdk/request/request_manager.go:67-100`](https://github.com/sprindigo-art/pasarpolis/blob/7355fb55a3e65c0166bf31cab81923d5519a83d9/go-sdk/request/request_manager.go#L67-L100))

Fix criteria: The tests obtain credentials from the environment, or are skipped when none are set. No real secret remains in the tree or history. Grepping for the redacted prefix returns only the documented placeholder.

(2) The disclosed secret stays usable until it is rotated on the API side.

Fix criteria: The `pasarpolis` testing-environment secret is revoked. Requests signed with the old value are rejected.

data.assessment:
The attacker is anyone who can reach port 8000, for example a party with access to the internal network, where the threat model places the unauthenticated `/metrics` endpoint. No login, user action or special setup is needed. The Docker image exposes port 8000 and runs `llen.py` directly, and the README publishes it with `-p 8000:8000`. Nothing in front of the exporter imposes a client timeout. The attacker needs no volume, because one idle socket is enough, and can re-open it at will.

Impact: The exporter stops serving `/metrics` for as long as the attacker holds the connection, so Prometheus and every other client get no response. No data is read or changed.

1. **attacker** opens a TCP connection to port 8000 and sends nothing. The attacker can also send the request line or headers one byte at a time, which has the same effect. ([`devops-redis-queue-length-exporter/Dockerfile:9-11`](https://github.com/sprindigo-art/pasarpolis/blob/7355fb55a3e65c0166bf31cab81923d5519a83d9/devops-redis-queue-length-exporter/Dockerfile#L9-L11))
2. **the server from `make_server`** accepts the connection and handles it inside `serve_forever`. The server has no `ThreadingMixIn`, so `process_request` runs `finish_request` in the same thread and only one connection is handled at a time. ([`devops-redis-queue-length-exporter/llen.py:39-40`](https://github.com/sprindigo-art/pasarpolis/blob/7355fb55a3e65c0166bf31cab81923d5519a83d9/devops-redis-queue-length-exporter/llen.py#L39-L40))
3. **the handler `WSGIRequestHandler.handle`** blocks in `self.rfile.readline(65537)` waiting for a complete request. `StreamRequestHandler.timeout` is `None` and the script sets no other timeout, so `settimeout()` is never called and the read has no deadline. ([`devops-redis-queue-length-exporter/llen.py:39-40`](https://github.com/sprindigo-art/pasarpolis/blob/7355fb55a3e65c0166bf31cab81923d5519a83d9/devops-redis-queue-length-exporter/llen.py#L39-L40))
4. **`serve_forever`** cannot return to accept new connections. The only worker is stuck on the idle client, so Prometheus scrapes of `my_app` time out. ([`devops-redis-queue-length-exporter/llen.py:34-37`](https://github.com/sprindigo-art/pasarpolis/blob/7355fb55a3e65c0166bf31cab81923d5519a83d9/devops-redis-queue-length-exporter/llen.py#L34-L37))
data.recommendation:
The HTTP server accepts one connection at a time and reads the request with no deadline, so an idle or slow client monopolises the only worker.

Fix criteria: A client that connects and never completes a request is dropped after a bounded time. It also does not prevent concurrent scrapes from being answered. To verify, hold an idle connection to port 8000 while a second client fetches `/metrics`. The second client must receive a 200 within the normal scrape timeout.
data.title: Single-threaded exporter with no read timeout: one idle connection blocks all scrapes

data.assessment:
The attacker is anyone who can read the public repository. They need no account, no prior privilege and no victim action. They copy the partner code and secret from `sdk.py:3`. Then they either uncomment the block and run it, or sign requests themselves the way `hmac_auth.py` does, with a fresh timestamp. They send the requests over the internet to the sandbox policy API. The report cannot check whether the secret is still valid, or whether it also works on testing or production hosts.

Impact: The attacker can act as partner `internal` on the sandbox policy API. They can create, validate, cancel and terminate policies. They can read policy status, document URLs and holder details for references they know, such as the one in `sdk.py`. Only the sandbox host is shown, so the data is largely integration data.

Subsequent-system impact: The affected system is the PasarPolis sandbox policy API, outside this repository. Production impact is not established, because only the sandbox host appears in the code. Actions possible there are creating, validating, cancelling and terminating policies, and reading status, document URLs and holder details for references the attacker knows.
data.description:
Anyone who can read the public repository can sign requests as the PasarPolis partner `internal` on the sandbox policy API. With that they can create, validate, cancel and terminate policies and read details of policies whose references they know. No login or victim action is needed. The cause is a real partner secret left in a commented-out `Client.init` call at `pasarpolis-sdk-python/sdk.py:3`.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  n1["anyone reading the public repository"]
  n2["sdk.py line 3 commented-out Client.init with partner secret"]
  n3["SDK signing and headers (hmac_auth.py, request_manager.py)"]
  n4["PasarPolis sandbox policy API"]
  n5["policies and holder data of partner internal"]
  n1 -->|"reads partner code and secret"| n2
  n1 -->|"uncomments block or signs requests itself"| n3
  n2 -->|"supplies the HMAC key"| n3
  n3 -->|"sends validly signed requests"| n4
  n4 -->|"lets caller act as internal"| n5

  class n4 component
  class n5 asset
```

1. **attacker** reads the partner code and secret in `pasarpolis-sdk-python/sdk.py`. Line 3 holds a commented-out `Client.init` call with partner code `internal`, a redacted credential and the host `https://integrations-sandbox.pasarpolis.io`. Commenting the line out does not remove it from the public repository. ([`pasarpolis-sdk-python/sdk.py:3`](https://github.com/sprindigo-art/pasarpolis/blob/7355fb55a3e65c0166bf31cab81923d5519a83d9/pasarpolis-sdk-python/sdk.py#L3))
2. **attacker** gets a ready target reference from the same commented block. The block calls `Policy.get_policy_status` for a concrete policy reference, so the attacker knows a reference to query. ([`pasarpolis-sdk-python/sdk.py:14-16`](https://github.com/sprindigo-art/pasarpolis/blob/7355fb55a3e65c0166bf31cab81923d5519a83d9/pasarpolis-sdk-python/sdk.py#L14-L16))
3. **attacker** signs requests with the leaked secret, either by uncommenting the block or by computing the signature directly. The secret is the only key of the HMAC-SHA256 signature, and the signer picks the timestamp, so a valid signature can be made for any request at any time. ([`pasarpolis-sdk-python/pasarpolis/request/auth/hmac_auth.py:21-23`](https://github.com/sprindigo-art/pasarpolis/blob/7355fb55a3e65c0166bf31cab81923d5519a83d9/pasarpolis-sdk-python/pasarpolis/request/auth/hmac_auth.py#L21-L23))
4. **the SDK request code in `request_manager.py`** sends the request with the `Partner-Code` and `Signature` headers. These two headers are the only authentication material, so the leaked pair is enough to identify the caller as `internal`. ([`pasarpolis-sdk-python/pasarpolis/request/request_manager.py:32-39`](https://github.com/sprindigo-art/pasarpolis/blob/7355fb55a3e65c0166bf31cab81923d5519a83d9/pasarpolis-sdk-python/pasarpolis/request/request_manager.py#L32-L39))
5. **sandbox policy API** accepts the requests as coming from partner `internal`. The report does not show server code. It infers acceptance from the header-only authentication and cannot confirm the secret is still valid.
data.recommendation:
(1) A real partner code and secret are committed in `pasarpolis-sdk-python/sdk.py:3` as a comment. Everyone who reads the repository can see the HMAC signing key.

Fix criteria: No real partner code and secret pair remains in `sdk.py` or anywhere in the tree or git history. Example scripts take credentials from the environment or configuration. Grepping the tree and history for the redacted prefix of the secret finds no match.

(2) The disclosed `internal` partner secret stays usable on the PasarPolis API until it is rotated.

Fix criteria: The `internal` partner secret is revoked and reissued on every environment where it was valid: sandbox, plus testing or production if it was reused there. A request signed with the old value is rejected.
data.title: Partner secret for `internal` partner committed in Python SDK sdk.py

data.assessment:
The attacker is anyone who can read the repository, which the threat model treats as public. They need no login, no access to PasarPolis systems and no victim action. They copy the secret and point the SDK, or any HTTP client that implements `auth/hmac.go`, at `integrations-sandbox.pasarpolis.io`. The attack works only if the key has not been rotated. The report cannot show from the code whether it was rotated after the commit.

Impact: The attacker fully assumes two partner identities on the sandbox integration API. They can read every policy record those partners can query, including names, document URLs and application numbers. They can also create, cancel or terminate policies under those partner codes. The code binds the keys to the sandbox host, where data is expected to be test data, so the loss is rated limited. The report says the impact would be high if production accepted the same secrets, but the code cannot establish that. The `endorsement_token` printed in the README is extra credential material from the same account. The report does not say what it unlocks beyond the README's description of it as the token required for authentication in case the endorsement flow is present.
data.description:
Anyone who can read the public repository can act as the partners `shopee` and `akseleran` on the PasarPolis sandbox integration API. They can read those partners' policy records and create, cancel or terminate policies. The only precondition is that the secrets have not been rotated. The secrets are committed in `go-sdk.v2/example/request_manager_example.go`, and the partner secret is the only key for the request signature.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  n1["anyone who can read the repository"]
  n2["request_manager_example.go with committed partner secrets"]
  n3["auth/hmac.go signing with partner secret"]
  n4["partner policy records on sandbox API"]
  n5["second factor beyond the secret"]
  n1 -->|"copies shopee and akseleran secrets"| n2
  n1 -->|"signs any request as the partner"| n3
  n3 -->|"valid Signature accepted"| n4
  n5 -->|"does not exist"| n3
  classDef actor stroke:#2563eb,stroke-width:2px
  classDef vulnerable_code stroke:#dc2626,stroke-width:2px
  classDef existing_control stroke:#16a34a,stroke-width:2px
  classDef missing_control stroke:#dc2626,stroke-width:2px,stroke-dasharray:5 5
  classDef asset stroke:#9333ea,stroke-width:2px
  classDef component stroke:#6b7280,stroke-width:1px
  class n1 actor
  class n2 vulnerable_code
  class n3 component
  class n4 asset
  class n5 missing_control
```

1. **attacker** reads the example file in the public repository. The file holds a live, uncommented `pasarpolis.InitClient` call with partner code `shopee` and its 36-character partner secret, bound to `https://integrations-sandbox.pasarpolis.io`. ([`go-sdk.v2/example/request_manager_example.go:43`](https://github.com/sprindigo-art/pasarpolis/blob/7355fb55a3e65c0166bf31cab81923d5519a83d9/go-sdk.v2/example/request_manager_example.go#L43))
2. **attacker** also copies the other committed secrets. A commented line holds the `akseleran` partner secret, and another commented line repeats the `shopee` secret. ([`go-sdk.v2/example/request_manager_example.go:11`](https://github.com/sprindigo-art/pasarpolis/blob/7355fb55a3e65c0166bf31cab81923d5519a83d9/go-sdk.v2/example/request_manager_example.go#L11))
3. **attacker** signs requests with the stolen secret. In `auth/hmac.go` the partner secret is the only HMAC-SHA256 key over verb, body MD5, content type, timestamp and path, so the attacker can mint a valid `Signature` header for any request, using the SDK or their own client. ([`go-sdk.v2/auth/hmac.go:39-45`](https://github.com/sprindigo-art/pasarpolis/blob/7355fb55a3e65c0166bf31cab81923d5519a83d9/go-sdk.v2/auth/hmac.go#L39-L45))
4. **attacker** queries known policy references to confirm the key works. The example also publishes two real policy references that belong to that partner, so `GetPolicyStatusV3` can be called on known records at once. ([`go-sdk.v2/example/request_manager_example.go:44`](https://github.com/sprindigo-art/pasarpolis/blob/7355fb55a3e65c0166bf31cab81923d5519a83d9/go-sdk.v2/example/request_manager_example.go#L44))
5. **sandbox API** accepts the signed requests as the partner. No second factor exists, so the attacker can read policy status and create, validate, cancel or terminate policies under those partner codes.
data.recommendation:
Real partner secrets for `shopee` and `akseleran`, partner codes, live policy references and an `endorsement_token` are embedded in the published `go-sdk.v2/example/` file and in `go-sdk.v2/README.md`. The tests already use the placeholder `<secret-key>`, so the example was missed.

Fix criteria: No real secret or token appears anywhere in `go-sdk.v2/example/` or `go-sdk.v2/README.md`, and only placeholders such as `<secret-key>` remain. The leaked `shopee` and `akseleran` secrets and the endorsement token are rotated or revoked on the PasarPolis side, and the values are purged from git history. Grepping the repository and its history for the prefixes `ff5ae273-`, `05d6dad6-` and `3555b77c` finds nothing. The API rejects the old values.
data.title: Live partner API secrets for Shopee and Akseleran committed in go-sdk.v2 example
